sections.subtitle: Drugo izdanje Block Talka: rotirajuća moderatorska palica i tema koja se nametnula sama
sections.screenshot_description: Voditelj Veljko Skenderija pozdravlja sugovornike Vedrana Mijatovića i Deana Rogulju na početku drugog izdanja
sections.content:
Drugo izdanje emisije **Block Talk** donosi novu organizaciju razgovora. Moderatorsku ulogu ovaj put preuzima **Veljko Skenderija**. U premijernom izdanju razgovor je vodio **Vedran Mijatović** s kanala „Moj Kripto“, a sljedeći tjedan palica prelazi u ruke **Deana Rogulje** s kanala „Kripto Evolucija“. Trojica autora tako se izmjenjuju u ulozi voditelja, a ostala dvojica u svakom izdanju sudjeluju kao sugovornici.

Skenderija se na početku ispričava gledateljima zbog promuklog glasa jer ga je „nešto ulovilo“. Rogulja odmah dobacuje da ga je „ulovio Binance“. Šala je ujedno i najava glavne teme. Voditelj otvara razgovor najvećim hakerskim napadom u povijesti kripto industrije: dok je ostatak svijeta spavao, kako slikovito kaže, „dečki iz Sjeverne Koreje marljivo su radili“ i s Binancea izvukli između **6,3 i 6,4 milijarde dolara**.

Prvo pitanje Skenderija upućuje Mijatoviću. Zanima ga kako se napad dogodio, koje hipoteze kruže javnošću i, kao najvažnije, može li takav *black swan* događaj gurnuti tržište u novi medvjeđi ciklus.
sections.subtitle_en: Second edition of Block Talk: rotating moderator baton and a topic that imposed itself
sections.screenshot_description_en: Host Veljko Skenderija greets interlocutors Vedran Mijatović and Dean Rogulja at the beginning of the second edition
sections.content_en:
The second edition of the show **Block Talk** brings a new organization of the conversation. The moderator role is taken over this time by **Veljko Skenderija**. In the premiere edition, the conversation was hosted by **Vedran Mijatović** from the channel "Moj Kripto", and next week the baton passes into the hands of **Dean Rogulja** from the channel "Kripto Evolucija". The three authors thus take turns in the role of host, while the other two participate in each edition as interlocutors.

Skenderija apologizes to the viewers at the beginning because of a hoarse voice, as "something caught" him. Rogulja immediately quips that "Binance caught" him. The joke is at the same time the announcement of the main topic. The host opens the conversation with the biggest hacker attack in the history of the crypto industry: while the rest of the world slept, as he picturesquely says, "the boys from North Korea worked diligently" and extracted between **6.3 and 6.4 billion dollars** from Binance.

Skenderija addresses the first question to Mijatović. He is interested in how the attack happened, what hypotheses are circulating in public, and, most importantly, whether such a *black swan* event can push the market into a new bear cycle.

sections.subtitle: Ulaz kroz stražnja vrata: kako je Lazarus grupa probila Binance
sections.screenshot_description: Vedran Mijatović objašnjava da hakeri ulaze kroz backdoorove, a ne kroz najčuvanija glavna vrata platforme
sections.content:
Mijatović najprije iznosi ono što se iz prakse zna o napadima na kripto platforme. Napadači nikad ne idu na „glavna vrata“, gdje je zaštita najjača. Traže *backdoorove*, plug-inove, aplikacije i druge dodatke koji su sa strane povezani s platformom, pa pokušavaju ući kroz njih.

Prema dosad dostupnim informacijama, isto se dogodilo i ovaj put. Napadači su hakirali **laptop jednog od Binanceovih inženjera** zaduženog za sigurnost, plaćanja i protokole, koji upravlja određenim ključevima. Mijatović napominje da u priči ima i složenijih tehničkih detalja povezanih s novim protokolima Ethereuma. Suština je ipak jednostavna: preko kompromitiranog računala omogućeno je istodobno izvršavanje golemog broja plaćanja s više računa. Iz burze je tako izvučena ogromna količina kripta, ponajviše u **stablecoinima**, ali i u raznim drugim kriptovalutama.

Iza napada, prema svemu poznatom, stoji **Lazarus grupa**, specijalni odred u Sjevernoj Koreji koji se bavi hakiranjem i iza kojeg su već veliki napadi. Mijatović navodi da su hakeri, po njegovim saznanjima, ukradena sredstva spojili sa sredstvima iz napada na **Bybit** od prije nekoliko mjeseci, pa je sve završilo na istoj adresi.

Za Sjevernu Koreju, ističe Mijatović, to je ozbiljan izvor prihoda. Riječ je o slabo razvijenom gospodarstvu, pa su „par milijardi dolara“ koje svako malo dođu na raspolaganje za tu zemlju vrlo značajni iznosi. Borba protiv takvih napada sve je teža jer danas postoje razvijeni AI modeli koji „rade čuda“. Ni oni ne moraju biti najnoviji: prema Mijatoviću, i slabiji kineski modeli otvorenog koda „rade totalne ludnice“.
sections.subtitle_en: Entry through the back door: how the Lazarus group breached Binance
sections.screenshot_description_en: Vedran Mijatović explains that hackers enter through backdoors, not through the platform's most guarded front door
sections.content_en:
Mijatović first presents what is known from practice about attacks on crypto platforms. Attackers never go to the "front door", where protection is strongest. They look for *backdoors*, plug-ins, applications, and other add-ons that are connected to the platform from the side, and then try to enter through them.

According to currently available information, the same happened this time. The attackers hacked the **laptop of one of Binance's engineers** in charge of security, payments, and protocols, who manages certain keys. Mijatović notes that there are also more complex technical details in the story connected with new Ethereum protocols. The essence is nonetheless simple: through the compromised computer, the simultaneous execution of a huge number of payments from multiple accounts was enabled. A huge amount of crypto was thus extracted from the exchange, mostly in **stablecoins**, but also in various other cryptocurrencies.

Behind the attack, according to everything known, stands the **Lazarus group**, a special squad in North Korea that deals with hacking and has major attacks behind it already. Mijatović states that the hackers, according to his information, merged the stolen funds with funds from the attack on **Bybit** from several months ago, so everything ended up at the same address.

For North Korea, Mijatović points out, this is a serious source of income. It is an underdeveloped economy, so the "few billion dollars" that become available every now and then are very significant amounts for that country. The fight against such attacks is increasingly difficult because today there are advanced AI models that "work wonders". They do not even have to be the newest: according to Mijatović, even weaker Chinese open-source models "do total craziness".

sections.subtitle: „Popapala maca, idemo dalje“: hack kao novo normalno
sections.screenshot_description: Veljko Skenderija pita može li napad gurnuti tržište u dublji bear market
sections.content:
Mijatović smatra da je ovaj napad nastavak „nekog novog normalnog“ u kojem će takvih incidenata biti sve više, i u kriptu i izvan njega. Podsjeća na godine u kojima se u kripto zajednici strahovalo od scenarija poput „Binance hacka“ ili „China bana“ jer bi takav događaj navodno izazvao kolaps. Da se ovo dogodilo prije nekoliko godina, kaže, „to bi bio opći potop“.

Danas je reakcija bitno blaža. Bitcoin je pao, ali Mijatović ocjenjuje da je pad u nekim normalnim okvirima kad se usporedi s naslovom o najvećem hacku u povijesti Binancea. Najvažnijim smatra to što su **sredstva korisnika sigurna**. Binance ima golem fond za zaštitu korisnika, a upravo je ta burza, kako kaže, i pokrenula praksu osnivanja takvih fondova. Ukradeni iznos čini otprilike **4 do 5 posto** tog fonda pa, prema njegovim riječima, nitko neće ostati bez novca. Zaključuje rezignirano: „popapala maca, idemo dalje i čekamo neki novi hack, nažalost“.

Skenderija traži preciznije: znači li to da napad ne može gurnuti tržište u dublji medvjeđi trend? Mijatović odgovara da sam događaj ne može. Tržište ga je, po njemu, već preživjelo. Problem bi nastao kad bi se hack poklopio s drugim negativnim okolnostima, primjerice makroekonomskim šokom, novim napadima ili ratovima. Tada bi mogao postati dio šire priče. „Morat ćemo se naučiti na takve stvari“, poručuje.

Voditelj daje i podatak o cijeni: Bitcoin se u tom trenutku nalazi na oko **77.000 dolara**. Prije nego što se saznalo za napad bio je na **80 do 81 tisuću**, što Skenderija s obzirom na okolnosti ocjenjuje „doista okej“.
sections.subtitle_en: „Cat ate it, let's move on“: the hack as the new normal
sections.screenshot_description_en: Veljko Skenderija asks whether the attack can push the market into a deeper bear market
sections.content_en:
Mijatović believes that this attack is a continuation of "some new normal" in which there will be more and more such incidents, both in crypto and outside it. He recalls the years in which the crypto community feared scenarios like the "Binance hack" or the "China ban" because such an event would allegedly cause a collapse. If this had happened several years ago, he says, "that would have been a general deluge".

Today the reaction is significantly milder. Bitcoin fell, but Mijatović assesses that the decline is within some normal bounds when compared to the headline about the biggest hack in the history of Binance. He considers the most important thing to be that **user funds are safe**. Binance has a huge fund for user protection, and precisely that exchange, as he says, initiated the practice of establishing such funds. The stolen amount constitutes approximately **4 to 5 percent** of that fund, so, according to his words, no one will be left without money. He concludes resignedly: "the cat ate it, let's move on and wait for some new hack, unfortunately".

Skenderija asks for more precision: does that mean that the attack cannot push the market into a deeper bear trend? Mijatović replies that the event alone cannot. The market, according to him, has already survived it. The problem would arise if the hack coincided with other negative circumstances, for example a macroeconomic shock, new attacks, or wars. Then it could become part of a broader story. "We will have to get used to such things", he states.

The host also gives data on the price: Bitcoin at that moment is at around **77,000 dollars**. Before the attack became known it was at **80 to 81 thousand**, which Skenderija assesses as "truly okay" given the circumstances.

sections.subtitle: Prijeti li Binanceu navala na isplate?
sections.screenshot_description: Dean Rogulja komentira rizik od bank runa i otvaranje isplata na Binanceu
sections.content:
Skenderija se zatim obraća Rogulji. Pita ga jesu li sredstva korisnika doista sigurna, kako tvrde iz Binancea, i koliko je realna opasnost od *bank runa*, odnosno masovne navale na isplate. Binance je, naime, najavio da će **isplate ponovno omogućiti u roku od 48 sati**.

Rogulja se slaže s Mijatovićem da bi, da se ovo dogodilo prvi put, nastao opći kaos. Riječ je o najvećoj mjenjačnici, ali tržište je već prošlo niz sličnih slučajeva. Navodi nedavni incident na **Bitgetu**, prošlogodišnji na **Bybitu** te brojne manje napade.

Nadovezuje se i na misao iz prvog izdanja emisije: tržištu je, rekao je tada, potreban jedan događaj koji će resetirati sentiment. „Eto ti ga!“, dobacuje Skenderija. Rogulja naglašava da nitko ne može unaprijed znati kakav će to događaj biti, ali upravo će on pokazati koliko je tržište otporno.

Osobno ne očekuje klasični bank run jer se radi o mjenjačnici, a ne o banci. Za usporedbu podsjeća na **ožujak 2023.**, kada su banke povezane s kriptom, uključujući **Silvergate**, propale u roku od dva do tri dana. Skenderija dodaje da su tada pukle tri regionalne banke vezane uz kripto industriju. Rogulja to opisuje kao razdoblje „velikog kolapsa i velikog straha“.

Ipak upozorava na specifičnost Binancea. Kao najveća burza s najviše korisnika, ima mnogo ljudi kojima je to jedini račun. Takav korisnik nema račun na Bitgetu ni na Bybitu, izbjegao je i slom **FTX-a** i dosad je imao „siguran Binance“. Ovakvu situaciju sada doživljava prvi put. Rogulja zato zaključuje da bank runa po njegovu mišljenju neće biti, ali bi kod dijela ljudi mogao nastati dodatni stres. Pritisak bi mogao osjetiti i sam Binance ako svi navale u trenutku kad se „otvori slavina za isplate“.
sections.subtitle_en: Does a rush on withdrawals threaten Binance?
sections.screenshot_description_en: Dean Rogulja comments on the risk of a bank run and the reopening of withdrawals on Binance
sections.content_en:
Skenderija then turns to Rogulja. He asks him whether user funds are truly safe, as claimed by Binance, and how real the danger of a *bank run*, that is, a massive rush on withdrawals, is. Binance has, namely, announced that it will **re-enable withdrawals within 48 hours**.

Rogulja agrees with Mijatović that, if this had happened for the first time, general chaos would have ensued. It is the largest exchange, but the market has already gone through a series of similar cases. He cites the recent incident on **Bitget**, last year's on **Bybit**, and numerous smaller attacks.

He also follows up on a thought from the first edition of the show: the market, he said then, needs one event that will reset sentiment. "There you have it!", Skenderija quips. Rogulja emphasizes that no one can know in advance what kind of event that will be, but precisely it will show how resilient the market is.

Personally he does not expect a classic bank run because it is an exchange, not a bank. For comparison he recalls **March 2023**, when banks connected with crypto, including **Silvergate**, collapsed within two to three days. Skenderija adds that three regional banks tied to the crypto industry cracked then. Rogulja describes that as a period of "great collapse and great fear".

Yet he warns about the specificity of Binance. As the largest exchange with the most users, it has many people for whom it is the only account. Such a user does not have an account on Bitget or Bybit, avoided also the collapse of **FTX**, and until now had a "safe Binance". They are now experiencing such a situation for the first time. Rogulja therefore concludes that there will not be a bank run in his opinion, but additional stress could arise for some people. The pressure could also be felt by Binance itself if everyone rushes at the moment when the "tap for withdrawals is turned on".

sections.subtitle: Centralizacija koja je spasila tri milijarde: utrka hakera s izdavateljima stablecoina
sections.screenshot_description: Vedran Mijatović objašnjava kako su izdavatelji stablecoina brzo zamrznuli ukradena sredstva
sections.content:
Skenderija Mijatoviću postavlja pitanje s, kako kaže, napola praktičnom, a napola filozofskom dimenzijom. Mijatović voli „lamentirati o decentralizaciji“, no u ovom se slučaju centralizacija pokazala korisnom. Centralizirani izdavatelji stablecoina, među kojima su **Circle** i **Tether**, zamrznuli su svoje tokene i tako spasili oko **3 milijarde dolara**.

Mijatović odgovara da je to bilo očekivano. Kad su sredstva dokazano ukradena i kad je oštećeni veliki akter poput Binancea, izdavatelji USDC-a i USDT-a reagiraju i blokiraju sredstva. Takva brzina, međutim, nije pravilo. Kad bi netko ukrao novac pojedincu ili nekoj manje poznatoj hrvatskoj banci, kontakt s Circleom ili Tetherom trajao bi danima, ako bi uopće bio uspješan. Ovdje se radilo o velikom događaju pa su reakcije bile brze.

Zato je haker imao vrlo malo vremena, možda pola sata ili tek nekoliko minuta, da izađe iz USDT-a i USDC-a. Mijatović opisuje njegove opcije:

- **Uniswap**, gdje je likvidnost vjerojatno najveća. Dovoljno je zamijeniti USDC za Ether, a kad je imovina u Etheru, „ne može mu nitko ništa“.
- Neka druga alternativna swap platforma.
- **Near Intents**, koji swapove izvodi drukčije od Uniswapa, ali ima povijest zamrzavanja sredstava.

Kod Uniswapa postoje dva problema. Platforma bi mogla biti obaviještena i blokirati transakcije, a uz to je *slippage* golem. Tko odjednom mijenja 100 milijuna dolara za Ether, zbog načina na koji funkcionira *bonding curve* može izgubiti i 30 do 40 posto. Haker je stoga birao između tri loša rješenja: mijenjati velike iznose i mnogo izgubiti, usitniti transakcije i izgubiti dragocjeno vrijeme dok mu blokiraju sredstva, ili otići na platformu za koju zna da je doista decentralizirana. Skenderija napominje da su napadači najviše koristili **Uniswap** i **Aave**. Mijatović odgovara da je Aave „posebna priča“, kojoj se vraća na kraju emisije.
sections.subtitle_en: Centralization that saved three billion: hackers' race against stablecoin issuers
sections.screenshot_description_en: Vedran Mijatović explains how stablecoin issuers quickly froze stolen funds
sections.content_en:
Skenderija poses a question to Mijatović with, as he says, a half-practical, half-philosophical dimension. Mijatović likes to "lament about decentralization", but in this case centralization proved useful. Centralized stablecoin issuers, among which are **Circle** and **Tether**, froze their tokens and thus saved around **3 billion dollars**.

Mijatović replies that this was expected. When funds are proven stolen and when the injured party is a large actor like Binance, the issuers of USDC and USDT react and block the funds. Such speed, however, is not the rule. If someone stole money from an individual or some lesser-known Croatian bank, contact with Circle or Tether would last for days, if it were successful at all. Here it was a major event, so reactions were fast.

That is why the hacker had very little time, perhaps half an hour or just a few minutes, to exit USDT and USDC. Mijatović describes his options:

- **Uniswap**, where liquidity is probably highest. It is enough to swap USDC for Ether, and once the asset is in Ether, "nobody can do anything to him".
- Some other alternative swap platform.
- **Near Intents**, which executes swaps differently from Uniswap, but has a history of freezing funds.

With Uniswap there are two problems. The platform could be notified and block transactions, and in addition *slippage* is huge. Whoever suddenly swaps 100 million dollars for Ether, due to the way the *bonding curve* works, can lose 30 to 40 percent. The hacker therefore chose between three bad solutions: swap large amounts and lose a lot, break up transactions and lose precious time while his funds are blocked, or go to a platform that he knows is truly decentralized. Skenderija notes that the attackers mostly used **Uniswap** and **Aave**. Mijatović replies that Aave is a "special story", to which he returns at the end of the show.

sections.subtitle: Thorchain i načelo da protokol ne pita odakle dolazi novac
sections.screenshot_description: Vedran Mijatović objašnjava zašto je Thorchain hakeru ostao kao jedina opcija i zašto nije blokirao swapove
sections.content:
Prema Mijatoviću, hakeru je na kraju ostao jedino **Thorchain**. Ta platforma izvodi takozvane *atomic swapove* na razini protokola, preko decentralizirano postavljenih *liquidity poolova*. Korisnik samo zatraži zamjenu, netko je izvrši „i ništa ne pita, i nije ga briga otkud je“.

Skenderija pita zašto Thorchain nije zaustavio transakcije kad za to navodno ima tehničku mogućnost. Mijatović potvrđuje da ta mogućnost postoji. Kad je sam protokol bio u opasnosti, Thorchain je zaustavio cijeli chain. Kod decentraliziranih sustava, kao i kod Bitcoina, takva odluka ipak traži **konsenzus svih sudionika**. Thorchain bi morao javno objaviti da je haker poslao milijardu dolara ukradenog novca i raspisati glasanje o zaustavljanju transakcija. Mijatović vjeruje da bi sudionici gotovo sigurno odbili. Načelo im je da ih ne zanima odakle dolazi pojedina transakcija niti zašto je hakiran Binance.

Usporedbu povlači s Bitcoinom. Kad bi se svi sudionici dogovorili da Bitcoina ne bude 21 milijun nego 100 milijuna, tako bi i bilo, ali šanse da do takvog dogovora dođe vrlo su male. Kod Thorchaina su se, kaže, ljudi dogovorili samo kad je napadnut sam protokol i kad ga je trebalo hitno spasiti. Ovaj put nisu, a vjerojatno neće ni ubuduće.

Na Skenderijino pitanje podržava li takav pristup Mijatović odgovara: „Da, naravno.“ Decentralizirani sustavi rade po tom principu. Slaba točka obično je istaknuti pojedinac, primjerice glavni developer kojeg se može uhititi ili pritisnuti. Thorchain je, međutim, ustrojen tako da ni on nema takve ovlasti. Može tek zamoliti sudionike koje osobno ne poznaje i koji mogu biti bilo gdje, od Irana do Australije. Ni uhićenjem ga se ne bi moglo natjerati da zaustavi transakcije.

Mijatović naglašava da takav protokol nije kažnjiv jer omogućuje **privatnost**, a privatnost je temeljno ljudsko pravo upisano u ustave i povelje Ujedinjenih naroda. Zlouporabu ilustrira usporedbom s automobilima: kradljivci ponekad bježe Hondom, ali to „nema veze s Hondom, Honda samo radi aute“. Skenderija analizu kratko komentira: „Super, gospodine Mijatoviću.“
sections.subtitle_en: Thorchain and the principle that the protocol does not ask where the money comes from
sections.screenshot_description_en: Vedran Mijatović explains why Thorchain remained as the hacker's only option and why it did not block swaps
sections.content_en:
According to Mijatović, in the end only **Thorchain** remained for the hacker. That platform executes so-called *atomic swaps* at the protocol level, via decentralized *liquidity pools*. The user only requests an exchange, someone executes it "and asks nothing, and does not care where it came from".

Skenderija asks why Thorchain did not stop transactions when it allegedly has the technical capability to do so. Mijatović confirms that this capability exists. When the protocol itself was in danger, Thorchain halted the entire chain. In decentralized systems, as with Bitcoin, such a decision nevertheless requires the **consensus of all participants**. Thorchain would have to publicly announce that a hacker sent a billion dollars of stolen money and call a vote on halting transactions. Mijatović believes that the participants would almost certainly refuse. Their principle is that they are not interested in where an individual transaction comes from, nor why Binance was hacked.

He draws a comparison with Bitcoin. If all participants agreed that there would be 100 million Bitcoins instead of 21 million, it would be so, but the chances of such an agreement happening are very small. With Thorchain, he says, people agreed only when the protocol itself was attacked and when it needed to be saved urgently. This time they did not, and they probably will not in the future either.

To Skenderija's question whether he supports such an approach, Mijatović replies: "Yes, of course." Decentralized systems work on that principle. The weak point is usually a prominent individual, for example a lead developer who can be arrested or pressured. Thorchain, however, is structured so that even he does not have such powers. He can only ask participants whom he does not know personally and who can be anywhere, from Iran to Australia. Even by arresting him, he could not be forced to stop transactions.

Mijatović emphasizes that such a protocol is not punishable because it enables **privacy**, and privacy is a fundamental human right inscribed in constitutions and charters of the United Nations. He illustrates the abuse by comparison with cars: thieves sometimes flee in a Honda, but that "has nothing to do with Honda, Honda just makes cars". Skenderija briefly comments on the analysis: "Great, Mr. Mijatović."

sections.subtitle: Gdje sada čuvati kripto? Ne sva jaja u istoj košari
sections.screenshot_description: Dean Rogulja odgovara na pitanje treba li sredstva držati na CEX-u, DEX-u ili u vlastitoj pohrani
sections.content:
Skenderija zatim podsjeća da probijene nisu bile samo mjenjačnice poput Bitgeta i Bybita, čiji je napad s oko milijardu i pol dolara dosad bio najveći, nego i niz *hardverskih novčanika*. Pita Rogulju gdje ljudi uopće trebaju držati sredstva. Traži i komentar izjave **Jeffa Kendricka** iz **Standard Chartereda** da bi ovakvi incidenti mogli ubrzati prelazak na decentralizirano trgovanje, odnosno na DEX-ove.

Rogulja se s tom izjavom ne slaže. Hackovi na mjenjačnicama nisu ugodni, ali korisnici velikih burzi na kraju su, barem u novije vrijeme, dobili svoj novac. Iznimka je FTX, a starije slučajeve poput **Mt. Goxa** ostavlja po strani. Istodobno se događaju i krađe s novčanika te napadi kroz ranjivosti različitih *bridgeova*. Rizik, dakle, postoji svugdje.

Rogulja priznaje da će dio ljudi nakon ovoga promijeniti pristup. Sam se vodi starim pravilom: **ne drži sva jaja u istoj košari**. Očekuje da će ulagači početi raspoređivati sredstva, dio na centraliziranim mjenjačnicama (CEX), a dio na decentraliziranima (DEX). Neke će ovakvi događaji potaknuti da preuzmu odgovornost za vlastita sredstva umjesto da ih povjere nekom drugom, kao što je slučaj s mjenjačnicama.

Navodi i primjer Binanceove veličine. Ako jedna mjenjačnica ima 200 milijuna korisnika, a druga 100 milijuna, dobar dio korisnika veće burze vjerojatno ni ne zna za drugu. Takvi bi se sada mogli „osokoliti“ i više istraživati vlastitu pohranu (*self custody*). Rogulja ipak ne vjeruje da će to preokrenuti trend.
sections.subtitle_en: Where to keep crypto now? Not all eggs in one basket
sections.screenshot_description_en: Dean Rogulja answers the question of whether funds should be kept on a CEX, a DEX, or in self-custody
sections.content_en:
Skenderija then recalls that it was not only exchanges like Bitget and Bybit, whose attack with about a billion and a half dollars was the biggest so far, that were breached, but also a series of *hardware wallets*. He asks Rogulja where people should keep funds at all. He also asks for a comment on the statement by **Jeff Kendrick** from **Standard Chartered** that such incidents could accelerate the transition to decentralized trading, that is, to DEXes.

Rogulja does not agree with that statement. Hacks on exchanges are not pleasant, but users of large exchanges ended up, at least in recent times, getting their money. The exception is FTX, while older cases like **Mt. Gox** he leaves aside. At the same time, thefts from wallets and attacks through vulnerabilities of various *bridges* are also occurring. Risk, therefore, exists everywhere.

Rogulja admits that some people will change their approach after this. He himself is guided by the old rule: **do not keep all eggs in one basket**. He expects investors to start distributing funds, part on centralized exchanges (CEX) and part on decentralized ones (DEX). Some will be prompted by such events to take responsibility for their own funds instead of entrusting them to someone else, as is the case with exchanges.

He also cites the example of Binance's size. If one exchange has 200 million users and another 100 million, a good portion of the users of the larger exchange probably does not even know about the other. Such people could now be "emboldened" and explore self-custody (*self custody*) more. Rogulja nevertheless does not believe that this will reverse the trend.

sections.subtitle: Banke kao treća opcija: kripto za „prosječnog Joea“
sections.screenshot_description: Dean Rogulja opisuje scenarij u kojem prosječan korisnik kupuje Bitcoin preko svoje banke
sections.content:
Rogulja upozorava na mogućnost koja se u raspravama često zaboravlja. Uz CEX i DEX s vremenom će nastati i **treća kategorija**: ljudi će kupovati top kriptovalute izravno preko banaka. Skenderija napominje da to već postoji u obliku ETF-ova, no Rogulja misli na više od toga. Voditelj potvrđuje da je, koliko se sjeća, **Deutsche Bank** prošli tjedan najavila nešto u tom smjeru.

Rogulja opisuje kako se takve usluge obično uvode. Nikad se ne počinje odjednom sa svim malim ulagačima. Prvo se krene od VIP klijenata i onih koji bolje poznaju investicijske prilike, a zatim se ponuda postupno spušta prema širem krugu. Tako je bilo i s drugim investicijskim proizvodima. U Hrvatskoj je, kako navodi, nedavno krenula **Zaba**, za sada putem ETF-ova.

Skrbnik će i dalje biti netko drugi, ali to „average Joea“, prosječnu osobu naviknutu na odlazak u banku, neće zanimati. Takva će osoba jednostavno reći: „Evo, kupi mi Bitcoin za 100 eura.“ Ne želi razmišljati gdje se i kako imovina pohranjuje. Želi je vidjeti u svom mobilnom bankarstvu i „to je cijela priča“.

Rogulja zato predviđa tri skupine korisnika:

- oni koji drže sredstva na **centraliziranim mjenjačnicama**,
- oni koji trguju preko **DEX-ova** i čuvaju imovinu u **vlastitoj pohrani**,
- oni koji imovinu povjeravaju **bankama**.

Protiv masovnog prelaska na vlastitu pohranu govore i nedavni problemi s **Ledgerom** i hladnim novčanicima. Za mnoge je takvo čuvanje „prestresno“. Rogulja opisuje tipičnog korisnika koji jednom uključi svoj Ledger, provjeri stanje i onda ga ne dira dvije-tri godine. Kad ga ponovno želi aktivirati, mora tražiti upute. Nema vremena svakodnevno pratiti promjene protokola, hackove, delistanja i stanje mjenjačnica. Skenderija zaključuje da je takav razvoj očekivan s obzirom na ulazak tradicionalnih financija (**TradFi**) u kripto, pa bi to bila „treća poluga“ čuvanja digitalne imovine.
sections.subtitle_en: Banks as the third option: crypto for the "average Joe"
sections.screenshot_description_en: Dean Rogulja describes a scenario in which an average user buys Bitcoin through their bank
sections.content_en:
Rogulja warns of a possibility that is often forgotten in discussions. Alongside CEX and DEX, over time a **third category** will also arise: people will buy top cryptocurrencies directly through banks. Skenderija notes that this already exists in the form of ETFs, but Rogulja means more than that. The host confirms that, as far as he remembers, **Deutsche Bank** announced something in that direction last week.

Rogulja describes how such services are usually introduced. One never starts all at once with all retail investors. First it starts from VIP clients and those who know investment opportunities better, and then the offering is gradually lowered toward a broader circle. It was like that with other investment products too. In Croatia, as he states, **Zaba** recently started, for now through ETFs.

The custodian will still be someone else, but the "average Joe", the average person used to going to the bank, will not care about that. Such a person will simply say: "Here, buy me Bitcoin for 100 euros." They do not want to think about where and how the asset is stored. They want to see it in their mobile banking and "that is the whole story".

Rogulja therefore predicts three groups of users:

- those who keep funds on **centralized exchanges**,
- those who trade via **DEXes** and keep assets in **self-custody**,
- those who entrust assets to **banks**.

Recent problems with **Ledger** and cold wallets also speak against a massive transition to self-custody. For many, such storage is "too stressful". Rogulja describes a typical user who turns on their Ledger once, checks the balance, and then does not touch it for two to three years. When they want to activate it again, they have to look for instructions. They do not have time to follow protocol changes, hacks, delistings, and the status of exchanges daily. Skenderija concludes that such a development is expected given the entry of traditional finance (**TradFi**) into crypto, so that would be the "third lever" of storing digital assets.

sections.subtitle: Najgori listopad od 2014.: Vedran Mijatović ne vjeruje više u stare cikluse
sections.screenshot_description: Vedran Mijatović objašnjava zašto ne želi predviđati kretanje cijene i zašto smatra da su se četverogodišnji ciklusi razbili
sections.content:
Razgovor se potom okreće cijeni. Skenderija podsjeća da se listopad u kripto zajednici voli nazivati „Uptober“, no to je, kaže, više *meme* nego stvarnost. Ako se ne dogodi čudo, Bitcoin će **drugu godinu zaredom imati crveni listopad**. Trenutačni rezultat od nešto više od **minus 7 posto** ujedno je najgori listopad od **2014.** Voditelj pita Mijatovića koliko je to loša najava za kraj godine i što očekuje do kraja 2026.

Mijatović odgovara iskreno: „Ne znam.“ Teško mu je cijene i dalje gledati kroz prizmu četverogodišnjih ciklusa koji su dosad bili prilično jasni: akumulacija, pa ludi *bull market*, pa veliki pad. Smatra da se taj obrazac razbio. Živimo, kaže, u vremenu nepredvidivih događanja u kojem se gotovo svaki dan događa nešto bez presedana. Sve se u svemiru načelno „rimuje“ i kreće u ciklusima, ali stara sezonska pravila, poput „Uptobera“, „sell in May and go away“ ili ljetnog zatišja, po njemu više ne funkcioniraju tako jednostavno.

Ipak smatra da **Bitcoin dobro stoji**. Danas ga podržavaju najveći svjetski financijski igrači, čak i oni poput **JP Morgana** koji su donedavno govorili da „ne valja“. Od najjačih financijskih institucija do svakodnevnog govora običnih ljudi, Bitcoin je postao normalna klasa imovine.

Rogulja tu ubacuje šaljivu ispravku: „Nisu svi. **Peter Schiff** je neumoran.“ Skenderija dodaje da Schiff po njemu ima osobni problem s **Michaelom Saylorom**, toliko ozbiljan da bi možda trebao posjetiti liječnika. Mijatović se slaže da „ima živopisnih likova“, među kojima spominje i **Warrena Buffetta**.

Vraćajući se trendovima, Mijatović zaključuje da je Bitcoin dobro pozicioniran. Kretat će se pod utjecajem makroekonomskih događanja i *black swan* događaja, ali bez dosadašnjih „nemogućih padova i likvidacija“. Ušao je, kaže, u zonu zrelog asseta, koliko god takva imovina može biti stabilna u makroekonomski sve nestabilnijem okruženju. Na izravno pitanje ide li cijena gore odgovara: „Načelno prema gore.“ Kojim tempom, ne zna. Ne vjeruje ni u uobičajene prognoze tipa „100.000 do kraja godine“ koje se ponavljaju svake jeseni.
sections.subtitle_en: Worst October since 2014: Vedran Mijatović no longer believes in old cycles
sections.screenshot_description_en: Vedran Mijatović explains why he does not want to predict price movement and why he believes the four-year cycles have broken
sections.content_en:
The conversation then turns to price. Skenderija recalls that October likes to be called "Uptober" in the crypto community, but that, he says, is more of a *meme* than reality. If a miracle does not happen, Bitcoin will **have a red October for the second year in a row**. The current result of slightly more than **minus 7 percent** is at the same time the worst October since **2014**. The host asks Mijatović how bad an announcement that is for the end of the year and what he expects by the end of 2026.

Mijatović answers honestly: "I do not know." It is difficult for him to continue looking at prices through the prism of four-year cycles that were quite clear until now: accumulation, then a crazy *bull market*, then a big fall. He believes that pattern has broken. We live, he says, in a time of unpredictable events in which almost every day something without precedent happens. Everything in the universe in principle "rhymes" and moves in cycles, but the old seasonal rules, like "Uptober", "sell in May and go away", or the summer lull, in his view no longer function so simply.

Yet he believes that **Bitcoin stands well**. Today it is supported by the world's largest financial players, even those like **JP Morgan** who until recently said that it "is no good". From the strongest financial institutions to the everyday speech of ordinary people, Bitcoin has become a normal asset class.

Rogulja inserts a humorous correction here: "Not everyone. **Peter Schiff** is tireless." Skenderija adds that Schiff in his view has a personal problem with **Michael Saylor**, so serious that he should perhaps visit a doctor. Mijatović agrees that "there are colorful characters", among whom he also mentions **Warren Buffett**.

Returning to trends, Mijatović concludes that Bitcoin is well positioned. It will move under the influence of macroeconomic events and *black swan* events, but without the previous "impossible drops and liquidations". It has entered, he says, the zone of a mature asset, as much as such an asset can be stable in an increasingly unstable macroeconomic environment. To the direct question of whether the price is going up, he replies: "In principle upward." At what pace, he does not know. Nor does he believe in the usual forecasts of the type "100,000 by the end of the year" that are repeated every autumn.

sections.subtitle: Prokletstvo midterm godina: što pokazuju mjesečni povrati
sections.screenshot_description: Dean Rogulja dijeli ekran s tablicom mjesečnih povrata Bitcoina i analizira listopade u midterm godinama
sections.content:
Skenderija od Rogulje traži tehničku analizu: gdje su zone podrške, koji su pomični prosjeci važni i očekuje li konsolidaciju, daljnji pad ili oporavak. „More pain“ ili, kako Rogulja dobacuje, „more gain“? Voditelj dodaje i potpitanje. Za nekoliko dana održavaju se **međuizbori u SAD-u**, koji su se u posljednja tri ciklusa poklapali s dvoznamenkastim postotnim padom BTC-a.

Rogulja dijeli ekran s tablicom **mjesečnih povrata Bitcoina** i napominje da namjerno ne čita brojke jer nije siguran koliko se dobro vide. Listopad će, kaže, s „99 posto šanse“ završiti negativno. U prošlim midterm godinama listopad je bio negativan **2014.** i **2018.** Jedina iznimka bila je **2022.**, ali su joj prethodili teški mjeseci. Uslijedio je i težak studeni, u kojem je postavljeno dno medvjeđeg tržišta.

Zaključuje da je svaka midterm godina dosad bila nezgodna za Bitcoin. Upozorava, međutim, na nešto što se često zaboravlja. U tim su godinama tradicionalna tržišta istodobno postizala rekorde. **S&P 500** je 2018. dosegnuo *all-time high*, iako je godina bila vrlo volatilna, a rekordi su padali i 2014. Jedina midterm godina u kojoj se medvjeđe tržište tradicionalnih dionica poklopilo s medvjeđim tržištem Bitcoina bila je 2022. Rogulja najavljuje da će se o tome detaljnije razgovarati drugom prilikom.

Iz toga izvodi svoju tezu. Midterm godinama uvijek je prethodio parabolični rast Bitcoina, pa je u njima „uvijek bilo što ispuhati“. **2025.** je, međutim, prema njegovim riječima, bila prva takva godina koja je završila negativno, s crvenom godišnjom svijećom. Skenderija podsjeća na nagli listopadski pad nakon rekorda od **126 tisuća dolara** i na rekordne likvidacije. Rogulja zato smatra da je ova situacija drukčija od prethodnih i da bi ostatak godine na kraju mogao biti pozitivan. Konkretnu prognozu ne daje. Ako Bitcoin dosegne 100.000 dolara do kraja godine, bit će, kaže, „puna šaka brade“, a završetak u gornjim devedesetima „odmah bi potpisao“.
sections.subtitle_en: The curse of midterm years: what monthly returns show
sections.screenshot_description_en: Dean Rogulja shares his screen with a table of Bitcoin monthly returns and analyzes Octobers in midterm years
sections.content_en:
Skenderija asks Rogulja for a technical analysis: where are the support zones, which moving averages are important, and does he expect consolidation, further decline, or recovery. "More pain" or, as Rogulja quips, "more gain"? The host also adds a follow-up question. In a few days, the **US midterm elections** take place, which in the last three cycles coincided with a double-digit percentage drop in BTC.

Rogulja shares his screen with a table of **Bitcoin monthly returns** and notes that he deliberately does not read the numbers because he is not sure how well they can be seen. October will, he says, with a "99 percent chance" end negatively. In past midterm years, October was negative in **2014** and **2018**. The only exception was **2022**, but it was preceded by difficult months. A difficult November also followed, in which the bottom of the bear market was set.

He concludes that every midterm year so far has been tricky for Bitcoin. He warns, however, about something that is often forgotten. In those years traditional markets simultaneously achieved records. The **S&P 500** reached an *all-time high* in 2018, although the year was very volatile, and records fell in 2014 as well. The only midterm year in which the bear market of traditional equities coincided with the bear market of Bitcoin was 2022. Rogulja announces that this will be discussed in more detail on another occasion.

From this he derives his thesis. Midterm years were always preceded by parabolic growth of Bitcoin, so in them "there was always something to deflate". **2025**, however, according to his words, was the first such year that ended negatively, with a red yearly candle. Skenderija recalls the sharp October drop following the record of **126 thousand dollars** and the record liquidations. Rogulja therefore believes that this situation is different from previous ones and that the rest of the year could ultimately be positive. He does not give a concrete forecast. If Bitcoin reaches 100,000 dollars by the end of the year, it will, he says, be "a full fist of beard", and an end in the upper nineties "he would sign immediately".

sections.subtitle: Od 77 do 65 tisuća: Roguljina karta podrški i otpora
sections.screenshot_description: Dean Rogulja na tjednom grafu Bitcoina pokazuje 21-tjednu eksponencijalnu pomičnu prosječnu cijenu i zone podrške
sections.content:
Na Skenderijin poziv Rogulja prelazi na **tjedni graf** cijene Bitcoina i izdvaja ključne razine:

- **21-tjedna eksponencijalna pomična prosječna cijena (21 EMA)**. Bitcoin je, kaže, vrlo često voli testirati. U silaznom trendu od listopada 2025. bilo je nekoliko pokušaja, a Bitcoin je istu razinu testirao i 2023. i ranije. Iako je izgledalo da cijena do nje neće doći, sada se nalazi upravo na njoj, u zoni od otprilike **76 do 77 tisuća dolara**. To je prva podrška.
- **72 do 74 tisuće dolara**, zona vrhova iz 2024., koju Rogulja na grafu označava zelenom bojom i smatra „prilično jakom podrškom“.
- **65 do 67 tisuća dolara**, koju naziva „zadnjom linijom obrane“. Spuštanje tamo približilo bi cijenu **200-tjednoj prosječnoj cijeni**. Rogulja ne vjeruje previše u taj scenarij i vidi ga kao krajnji minimum ako stvari krenu u krivom smjeru.

U blizini trenutačnih cijena je i **50 SMA**, ali kaže da se njime ne bi previše zamarao. Prema gore ključni je otpor u zoni **84 do 86 tisuća dolara**, gdje se cijena „mučila“ prethodnih dana i koju na kraju nije uspjela probiti.
sections.subtitle_en: From 77 to 65 thousand: Rogulja's map of supports and resistances
sections.screenshot_description_en: Dean Rogulja shows the 21-week exponential moving average price and support zones on the Bitcoin weekly chart
sections.content_en:
At Skenderija's invitation, Rogulja moves to the **weekly chart** of the Bitcoin price and singles out key levels:

- **21-week exponential moving average price (21 EMA)**. Bitcoin, he says, likes to test it very often. In the downtrend from October 2025 there were several attempts, and Bitcoin tested the same level in 2023 and earlier. Although it looked like the price would not reach it, now it is sitting right on it, in the zone of roughly **76 to 77 thousand dollars**. That is the first support.
- **72 to 74 thousand dollars**, the zone of tops from 2024, which Rogulja marks in green on the chart and considers "fairly strong support".
- **65 to 67 thousand dollars**, which he calls the "last line of defense". Descending there would bring the price closer to the **200-week average price**. Rogulja does not believe too much in that scenario and sees it as an extreme minimum if things head in the wrong direction.

Near current prices is also the **50 SMA**, but he says he would not bother too much with it. Upward, key resistance is in the zone of **84 to 86 thousand dollars**, where the price "struggled" in previous days and which in the end it failed to break through.

sections.subtitle: Milijun dolara po Bitcoinu: moguće, ali uz zadršku inflacije
sections.screenshot_description: Veljko Skenderija predstavlja dugoročne prognoze cijene Bitcoina analitičara Willyja Wua i tvrtke Bitwise
sections.content:
Pri kraju emisije Skenderija otvara temu dugoročnih prognoza. Analitičar **Willy Wu** nedavno je testirao model s **10.000 simulacija**. Medijanski scenarij, ni medvjeđi ni bikovski, predviđa da će Bitcoin do **2028.** dosegnuti između **241 i 413 tisuća dolara**, a do **2033.** **milijun dolara**. **Bitwise** je pak dan-dva ranije povisio desetogodišnju prognozu za BTC s **1,3 na 1,6 milijuna dolara**. Voditelj pita sugovornike vjeruju li u takve razine u svega nekoliko godina.

Mijatović ih ne isključuje. Ne bi se kladio da će se ostvariti, ali ne bi se ni čudio. Milijun dolara po Bitcoinu u doglednom roku smatra zamislivim scenarijem, s obzirom na razinu adopcije i na to koliko se Bitcoin po svojoj naravi razlikuje od fiat valuta i njihove inflacije. Takvu bi razinu, po njemu, mogao izazvati *black swan* događaj, primjerice s dolarom, ili makroekonomski potres. Jednako je moguć i postupan rast. Dodaje važnu napomenu: milijun dolara za deset godina neće vrijediti koliko danas i njime će se moći kupiti puno manje. Ipak, riječ je o velikoj okrugloj brojci i psihološkoj granici.

Rogulja se posebno nadovezuje na inflacijski argument. Ako inflacija bude 10 do 15 posto godišnje ili više, milijun dolara „neće biti baš neki novac“. Cilj ulaganja, ističe, jest **nadmašiti inflaciju**. Tko to uspije, sačuvao je vrijednost. Prognozu ne smatra nerealnom, ali se ne bi kladio u nju. Kao vjerojatnu vidi je tek u scenariju hiperinflacije. O modelima je skeptičan: „možemo ih napraviti tisuću“, a na kraju će se dogoditi „tisuću i prva stvar“. Savršenog modela nema jer su svijet i tržišta kaotični. Skenderija sažima njegov stav: moguće, ali ne i vjerojatno. Rogulja to potvrđuje.
sections.subtitle_en: A million dollars per Bitcoin: possible, but with an inflation caveat
sections.screenshot_description_en: Veljko Skenderija presents long-term Bitcoin price forecasts by analyst Willy Wu and the firm Bitwise
sections.content_en:
Toward the end of the show, Skenderija opens the topic of long-term forecasts. Analyst **Willy Wu** recently tested a model with **10,000 simulations**. The median scenario, neither bear nor bull, predicts that Bitcoin will by **2028** reach between **241 and 413 thousand dollars**, and by **2033** **one million dollars**. **Bitwise**, on the other hand, a day or two earlier raised its ten-year forecast for BTC from **1.3 to 1.6 million dollars**. The host asks the interlocutors whether they believe in such levels in just a few years.

Mijatović does not rule them out. He would not bet that they will come true, but he would not be surprised either. A million dollars per Bitcoin in the foreseeable future he considers an imaginable scenario, given the level of adoption and how much Bitcoin by its nature differs from fiat currencies and their inflation. Such a level, according to him, could be triggered by a *black swan* event, for example with the dollar, or a macroeconomic earthquake. A gradual rise is equally possible. He adds an important note: a million dollars in ten years will not be worth what it is today and much less will be purchasable with it. Nevertheless, it is a large round number and a psychological barrier.

Rogulja particularly follows up on the inflation argument. If inflation is 10 to 15 percent annually or more, a million dollars "will not really be much money". The goal of investing, he points out, is to **outperform inflation**. Whoever succeeds in that has preserved value. He does not consider the forecast unrealistic, but he would not bet on it. He sees it as probable only in a hyperinflation scenario. About models he is skeptical: "we can make a thousand of them", and in the end "the thousand and first thing" will happen. There is no perfect model because the world and markets are chaotic. Skenderija summarizes his position: possible, but not probable. Rogulja confirms this.

sections.subtitle: Zašto raste interes za privacy coine: Monero naspram Zcasha
sections.screenshot_description: Vedran Mijatović odgovara na pitanje gledatelja o rastu interesa za privacy coine
sections.content:
Za kraj Skenderija prenosi pitanje gledatelja: odakle u posljednjih godinu dana toliki interes za *privacy coine*? **Zcash** „divlja“, a ni **Monero** nema lošu izvedbu.

Mijatović vidi dva glavna pokretača. Prvi je **pritisak regulatora**. Korisnike „na svakom ćošku“ traže KYC podatke za bilo kakvu transakciju ili korištenje aplikacija. Te podatke ljudi moraju predati po zakonu, a kad ih netko ukrade, „a ukrade im svaki dan“, nitko ne odgovara. Taj nesrazmjer stvara osjećaj nepravde i potrebu za zaštitom privatnosti.

Drugi je pokretač **poslovna logika**. Nijedna velika institucija ni tvrtka neće slati novac javno i transparentno. Banka ili tvrtka ne želi da svi vide da je nekome poslala 10.000 eura. Kako Skenderija napominje, na blockchainu se sve vidi. Blockchain je po prirodi transparentan, pa su potrebni posebni coini koji čuvaju privatnost.

Najstariji i najpoznatiji je **Monero**, čiju privatnost Mijatović opisuje kao neprobojnu: iz protokola se ne može saznati koliko je, kome i kada poslano. Za **Zcash** kaže da je tehnološki dobro napravljen, ali da mu izvedba nije savršena jer transakcije **nisu privatne po zadanim postavkama**. Privatnost je opcija koju korisnik sam mora uključiti (*opt-in*). Mijatović to otvoreno naziva prevarom: projekt se reklamira kao privacy chain, a u praksi je privatno manje od 30 posto transakcija. Zcash to opravdava usklađenošću s regulatorima, no Mijatoviću se to ne sviđa. Kao dokaz navodi da hakeri, kad žele skloniti novac, koriste Monero ili Thorchain, a ne Zcash.

Zcash po njemu jaše na valu hypea, možda uz podršku velikih ulagača, i mogao bi još iznenaditi cijenom, ali među privacy coinima mu „nije u prvom redu“. Dodaje da i **Ethereum** radi na privatnim transakcijama na razini protokola jer financijski svijet ne želi potpuno otvorene financije. Zaključuje da je privatnost temeljno ljudsko pravo zajamčeno ustavima civiliziranih zemalja te poveljama Ujedinjenih naroda i Europske unije. Nikoga, kaže, ne treba pitati zašto želi privatne transakcije.
sections.subtitle_en: Why interest in privacy coins is growing: Monero versus Zcash
sections.screenshot_description_en: Vedran Mijatović answers a viewer's question about the growth of interest in privacy coins
sections.content_en:
In conclusion, Skenderija conveys a viewer's question: where has so much interest in *privacy coins* come from in the past year? **Zcash** is "going wild", and **Monero** does not have a bad performance either.

Mijatović sees two main drivers. The first is **regulatory pressure**. Users "on every corner" are asked for KYC data for any kind of transaction or application usage. People must hand over this data by law, and when someone steals it, "and they steal it from them every day", no one is held accountable. That imbalance creates a sense of injustice and a need for privacy protection.

The second driver is **business logic**. No large institution or company will send money publicly and transparently. A bank or company does not want everyone to see that it sent someone 10,000 euros. As Skenderija notes, everything is visible on the blockchain. The blockchain is by nature transparent, so special coins that preserve privacy are necessary.

The oldest and most famous is **Monero**, whose privacy Mijatović describes as impenetrable: from the protocol it cannot be learned how much was sent, to whom, or when. About **Zcash** he says that it is technologically well made, but that its execution is not perfect because transactions **are not private by default**. Privacy is an option that the user must turn on themselves (*opt-in*). Mijatović openly calls that a scam: the project advertises itself as a privacy chain, and in practice fewer than 30 percent of transactions are private. Zcash justifies this with compliance with regulators, but Mijatović does not like that. As proof, he states that hackers, when they want to hide money, use Monero or Thorchain, not Zcash.

Zcash in his view rides on the wave of hype, perhaps with the support of large investors, and could still surprise in price, but among privacy coins it is "not in the front row" for him. He adds that **Ethereum** is also working on private transactions at the protocol level because the financial world does not want completely open finance. He concludes that privacy is a fundamental human right guaranteed by the constitutions of civilized countries and charters of the United Nations and the European Union. No one, he says, needs to be asked why they want private transactions.

sections.subtitle: Digitalni euro kao gorivo otpora i privacy priče kroz cikluse
sections.screenshot_description: Dean Rogulja govori o CBDC-ovima, digitalnom euru i privacy coinima iz prethodnih ciklusa
sections.content:
Rogulja se slaže s Mijatovićem i dodaje još jedan razlog. Sve se više govori o digitalnim nacionalnim valutama, odnosno o **CBDC-ovima**, kako ih precizira Mijatović. Prvenstveno spominje **digitalni euro**. Što je takvih projekata više, to su veći otpor i želja ljudi da izađu iz tog sustava.

Podsjeća i da privacy coini nisu nova pojava. Svaki ciklus, bilo bikovski ili medvjeđi, imao je svoju privacy priču:

- u ciklusu 2021. isticao se **Pirate Chain** (oznaka ARRR), a pojavio se i meme coin koji je parodirao Monero,
- u razdoblju 2017. i 2018., koliko se sjeća, to je bio **Verge** (oznaka XVG).

Ti su projekti i danas aktivni i imaju svoju priču. Hype je, kaže, uvijek postojao, a pitanje je samo koji će projekti opstati i koliko će doista pokrivati potrebu za privatnošću. Za sada je najkompletniji **Monero**. Zcash „baš i nije to to“, ali će na krilima hypea ovaj ciklus vjerojatno donijeti još dva-tri pobjednika po prinosima. Po stvarnoj uporabi Rogulja očekuje da će opstati možda dva glavna projekta.

Skenderija zatim spominje **Midnight**, novi projekt povezan s **Cardanom**, koji je opisao kao novi L2. Njegov tvorac tvrdi da će biti veći od Zcasha. Voditelj s rezervom dodaje da je to ipak njegov vlastiti blockchain pa će se tek vidjeti.
sections.subtitle_en: Digital euro as fuel for resistance and the privacy story across cycles
sections.screenshot_description_en: Dean Rogulja speaks about CBDCs, the digital euro, and privacy coins from previous cycles
sections.content_en:
Rogulja agrees with Mijatović and adds one more reason. There is more and more talk about digital national currencies, that is, about **CBDCs**, as Mijatović specifies them. He primarily mentions the **digital euro**. The more such projects there are, the greater the resistance and desire of people to exit that system.

He also recalls that privacy coins are not a new phenomenon. Every cycle, whether bull or bear, had its privacy story:

- in the 2021 cycle, **Pirate Chain** (ticker ARRR) stood out, and a meme coin parodying Monero also appeared,
- in the period of 2017 and 2018, as far as he remembers, that was **Verge** (ticker XVG).

Those projects are active even today and have their story. Hype, he says, has always existed, and the only question is which projects will survive and how much they will truly cover the need for privacy. For now, the most complete is **Monero**. Zcash "is not really quite it", but on the wings of hype this cycle will probably bring another two or three winners by returns. By actual usage, Rogulja expects that perhaps two main projects will survive.

Skenderija then mentions **Midnight**, a new project connected with **Cardano**, which he described as a new L2. Its creator claims it will be bigger than Zcash. The host adds with reserve that it is nevertheless its own blockchain, so it remains to be seen.

sections.subtitle: „Hack 2.0“: kako je haker iskoristio Aave za pranje ukradenog novca
sections.screenshot_description: Vedran Mijatović naknadno objašnjava kako je haker iskoristio DeFi protokol Aave za izvlačenje Ethera
sections.content:
Skenderija se već zahvaljuje gostima, no Mijatović se vraća na Binanceov hack. Želi dodati, kako kaže, zanimljiv detalj koji se prvi put dogodio u nekom napadu.

Haker je, dok je birao kako se na brzinu riješiti stablecoina prije zamrzavanja, iskoristio najveći DeFi protokol, **Aave**. Na njega je deponirao ukradeni USDT kao **kolateral** i na temelju njega posudio **Ether**. Tako je došao do Ethera u vrijednosti od otprilike **75 posto** iznosa kolaterala i s njim dalje može slobodno raspolagati. Na taj je način, prema Mijatoviću, ukradenu vrijednost izvukao iz stablecoina koji su mu prijetili blokadom i zapravo je oprao.

To pokazuje, kaže Mijatović, da napadači „jako dobro znaju što rade“ i vješto koriste tehnologiju. Takav pristup nazvao je „hack 2.0“.

Skenderija se zatim zahvaljuje Mijatoviću i Rogulji te najavljuje novo druženje za tjedan dana. Gledatelje poziva da u komentarima šalju pitanja i prijedloge tema, uz poruku da se emisija vraća „za sedam dana na istom mjestu u isto vrijeme“.
sections.subtitle_en: „Hack 2.0“: how the hacker used Aave to launder stolen money
sections.screenshot_description_en: Vedran Mijatović subsequently explains how the hacker used the DeFi protocol Aave to extract Ether
sections.content_en:
Skenderija is already thanking the guests, but Mijatović returns to the Binance hack. He wants to add, as he says, an interesting detail that happened for the first time in an attack.

The hacker, while choosing how to quickly get rid of stablecoins before the freeze, utilized the largest DeFi protocol, **Aave**. Onto it he deposited the stolen USDT as **collateral** and based on it borrowed **Ether**. He thus obtained Ether in the value of approximately **75 percent** of the collateral amount and can freely dispose of it further. In that way, according to Mijatović, he extracted the stolen value from the stablecoins that threatened him with a freeze and effectively laundered it.

This shows, Mijatović says, that the attackers "know very well what they are doing" and skillfully utilize technology. He termed such an approach "hack 2.0".

Skenderija then thanks Mijatović and Rogulja and announces a new gathering in a week. He invites viewers to send questions and topic suggestions in the comments, with the message that the show returns "in seven days at the same place at the same time".
